calibration.outdated_warning_banner: This profile is outdated — recalibrate it so everything works correctly.
calibration.capture_confidence_low: Too ambiguous — tilt sharply along one axis
calibration.confirm_hint: Rotate the device in your hands — 3D model should move in perfect sync.
calibration.disconnect_alert_desc: Device connection lost or screen turned off. Check the connection during calibration.
calibration.disconnect_reconnected_toast: Device connected. Click “Record” to retry the step.
calibration.err_axes_inconsistent: Axes are inconsistent with each other.
calibration.error_ambiguous: Ambiguous motion (diagonal tilt). Tilt strictly along one axis.
calibration.error_ambiguous_tilt: Device is tilted. Place device on a flat surface.
calibration.error_grip_changed: Device grip changed between steps. Hold device consistently throughout all tests.
calibration.error_inconsistent_axes: Motion axes are inconsistent with each other. Please recalibrate.
calibration.error_moved_during_rest: Device moved during rest calibration. Keep device perfectly still.
calibration.error_opposite_direction: Device was tilted in the opposite direction. Follow the on-screen prompt.
calibration.error_too_few_samples: Too few sensor samples. Check device connection.
calibration.error_too_weak: Motion too weak. Tilt device more decisively.
calibration.first_connect_desc: This device is likely connecting for the first time. We strongly recommend calibrating it by clicking the button below and creating a profile for it!
calibration.manual_hint: Choose axis mapping and test on the 3D model on the right
calibration.no_signal: No signal from device. Check connection.
calibration.report_copied_toast: Full test report copied to clipboard!
calibration.res_all_done: Calibration complete! Gamepad axes: Pitch: **{p}** • Yaw: **{y}** • Roll: **{r}**
calibration.save_overwrite_note: Caution: if the selected slot already contains a profile, it will be overwritten.
calibration.save_overwrite_warn: Warning: slot {slot} already contains profile "{name}" and will be overwritten.
calibration.save_slot_hint: Select slot and configure profile parameters:
calibration.step0_caption: Place your device on the table in gaming grip
calibration.step0_desc: Place your device still on the desk (in the same grip and orientation you plan to play in) and click **Record Stillness**. Gyroscope drift will be measured and the resting gravity vector will be recorded for accurate spatial alignment.
calibration.step1_desc: Tilt device forward and back, like nodding. Click **Start Capture** and smoothly tilt the top edge forward.
calibration.step2_desc: Bank device to the right like an airplane wing in a turn. Click **Start Capture**.
calibration.step3_caption: Twist and tilt the device together, pausing a second between moves
calibration.step3_desc: Pick up the device and rotate it in different, non-repeating directions, **combining a tilt with a twist at the same time** (plain forward/back and side-to-side tilts alone won't work) — as shown on the 3D model on the right. Pause for a second between moves. The system will physically work out how the device's accelerometer is oriented relative to its gyroscope. Skipping this can leave gravity reading on the wrong axis in-game.
calibration.step_hint: Watch the 3D animation on the right and mirror the motion
calibration.align_already_desc: This relation was already determined and saved to the profile: **{mapping}**
calibration.align_fail_desc: Not enough confident moves. Plain forward/back and side-to-side tilts alone aren't enough — make sure to ADD A TWIST to the device (like unscrewing a cap), combined with the tilt, and pause for a second between moves.
calibration.align_status_recording: Twist and tilt the device together, pausing between moves
calibration.subtitle: Map your device's axes to gamepad axes
calibration.title: Axis Calibration
calibration.view_disclaimer: 3D orientation may differ from your physical grip
calibration.mount_ok: The sensor is mounted at a {tilt}° tilt (forward {fwd}, right {right}). The gyroscope confirmed it ({check}° deviation). The correction rotates gyro and accelerometer together: neutral becomes level and horizontal turns stop leaking into tilt.
calibration.mount_small: The sensor is mounted level ({tilt}° tilt) — no correction needed.
calibration.mount_too_large: Resting tilt is {tilt}° — too much for a tilted board: the pad was probably not flat during the Rest step. No correction is applied. To get one, recalibrate on a flat surface.
calibration.mount_inconsistent: The accelerometer reads a {tilt}° tilt, but the gyroscope does not confirm it ({check}° off). This is most likely the accelerometer's own zero offset (up to 3–5° on an MPU-6050), not a tilted board. Rotating the axes would only hurt, so no correction is applied. Nothing to do.
calibration.mount_no_data: Not enough data to measure the mount tilt.
calibration.align_status_refining: Enough data — refining. Make a couple more moves in other directions
calibration.mount_profile_tip: Correction for the sensor board being mounted tilted in the case, measured at calibration and confirmed by the gyroscope. Turn it off to output the sensor axes as they are.
calibration.delete_profile_desc: This profile’s calibration will be removed permanently and its slot freed.

ui.bench_offline_desc: Connect a device to see the response in real time
ui.debug_panel_tip: A separate window (its own process, about 100 MB while open): the main window's FPS and frame time, CPU, RAM, sensor and ping with graphs, start phases, warnings and errors. When on, it starts before everything else and sees the start. Ctrl+Shift+Alt+D in the PhoneGyro window opens or closes it for now.
ui.debug_log_tip: Writes logs/debug.log (data folder): a session header, start phases, a summary line a second, warnings and errors. When on, it starts before everything else. Past 5 MB the file starts over.
ui.reset_all_desc: Everything on this screen goes back to its default. Theme, language and the DSU MAC address stay.
ui.scan_sub: Both devices on the same Wi‑Fi. Safari or Chrome opens the controller.
ui.no_profiles: No saved profiles yet. Calibrate the device.
ui.soon_desc: This section is moving to the new interface.
ui.stats_eco_desc: Pause rendering when window is inactive
ui.stats_charts_desc: Turn off to save resources on drawing
ui.stats_usb_tip: A step-by-step check of the controller's USB link, top to bottom. All green means all good.
ui.stats_usb_l1_tip: The port the controller is on and the link speed. Good: the port is found and open.
ui.stats_usb_l2_tip: How data flows: frames per second and whether any are lost or damaged. Good: no losses and no errors.
ui.stats_usb_l3_tip: Firmware version and sensor settings reported by the controller. Good: they are there and keep updating.
ui.stats_usb_l5_tip: Whether the controller has a reset button and how many times it was pressed.
ui.stats_offline_tip: Connect a device over Wi‑Fi or USB
ui.stats_quality_tip: Overall link score for the last few seconds: counts losses, delays, hiccups and rate. 80–100 is great, 50–79 is fine, below 50 the link is poor.
ui.stats_tail_tip: The longest gaps between data over the last half minute. Shows rare hiccups that averages hide. Up to 15 ms is good; over 50 ms you will feel jerks in the game. “Step” is the usual gap between data.
ui.stats_loss_merged_tip: How many packets got lost on the way. Good: 0. If it keeps growing, the link drops out: move closer to the router or try another cable.
ui.stats_drift_tip: How much the gyro “drifts” while the device lies still. The closer to zero, the better. If it is clearly above zero, run the calibration.
ui.stats_noise_tip: How much the signal shakes while the device lies still. Lower means smoother motion in the game. “Stable” is great, “Jitter” is acceptable.
ui.stats_gravity_tip: The gravity the sensor sees. At rest it should be about 1.00. If it is clearly off, the tilt sensor is slightly off too.
ui.stats_omega_tip: How fast you are rotating the device right now, and the fastest turn over the last minute. About zero at rest.
ui.stats_session_tip: How long the connection has lasted, how many packets arrived, how many got lost and how much data was sent.
ui.splash_tip: A short intro when PhoneGyro starts (about 3 seconds). Turn it off to open the window at once.
ui.cal_matrix_note: How the sensor axes (columns X, Y, Z) became the game axes: rows P — Pitch, Y — Yaw, R — Roll.

firewall.label: Windows Firewall
firewall.tip: The phone connects to the PC over Wi‑Fi, so Windows Firewall has to let incoming connections to PhoneGyro through. Windows asks once, on the first launch. If that window was closed or cancelled, the phone cannot connect and Windows never asks again. You can create the rule by hand; the docs explain how. The permission belongs to the file: a new PhoneGyro.exe in another folder is asked about again. The USB controller does not need it.
firewall.docs_heading: The phone cannot connect: Windows Firewall
firewall.alert_text:
> [!CAUTION]
> Windows Firewall does not let the phone connect to PhoneGyro, so the phone cannot connect. The USB controller is not affected.

Create an allow rule by hand, once. It takes about a minute; the docs show how.
firewall.alert_public: Windows marks your network as public; enable the rule for it too.
firewall.state_waiting: Waiting for your answer in the Windows prompt…

live_debug.cam_orbit_hint: Drag LMB to orbit • Scroll to zoom
live_debug.eco_desc: Pause rendering when window is inactive
live_debug.no_phone_desc: Connect a device to stream motion sensor data
live_debug.recenter_desc: Instantly resets virtual orientation to neutral baseline
live_debug.stats_dsu_clients_tip: How many emulators are receiving our data right now. If 0, the emulator is not running or not set up to use us.
live_debug.stats_hover_hint: Click a card to reveal description
live_debug.stats_in_hz_tip: How many times per second data arrives from the device. Good: a flat line with no dips. Dips mean the device briefly fell behind (the phone slept or was busy).
live_debug.stats_jitter_tip: How unevenly data arrives. A flat line near the bottom is good. Teeth and spikes mean the link stutters and motion in the game may shake.
live_debug.stats_latency_tip: How long data takes to travel from the phone to the PC. Lower means the game reacts to your motion faster. Up to 10 ms is great, up to 30 ms is fine. Frequent spikes mean Wi-Fi trouble. Not shown for USB.
live_debug.stats_loss_tip: Losses on the link from the controller to the computer. For USB — lost frames by sequence number; for the phone — merged and lost sensor samples. No data (n/a) means the source does not report it (old phone page).
live_debug.stats_modal_desc: Recording stopped (1 min limit reached or stopped manually). Would you like to save the .csv data file to disk?
live_debug.stats_out_gyro_tip: What the game finally gets, after all processing. If something is wrong here, the game feels it.
live_debug.stats_out_hz_tip: How many times per second we send data to the emulator. It should be about the same as what arrives from the device. If clearly lower, the app is falling behind.
live_debug.stats_pipe_latency_tip: How long the app itself spends on the data before sending it to the emulator. Usually under 1 ms, which you will not notice.
live_debug.stats_raw_accel_tip: How the device feels tilt and bumps, before our processing. At rest one line sits near 1 or −1 (that is gravity), the others in the middle.
live_debug.stats_raw_gyro_tip: How the device itself feels rotation, before our processing. Rotate it and the lines move; hold it still and they rest in the middle. If they shake while still, the sensor itself is noisy.

setup.android_desc: No certificate installation needed on Android. Open the controller address directly in Chrome.
setup.android_hint: Tap the chip or scan the QR code above to copy the link.
setup.disclosure_body_1: **What am I installing?** A small security certificate, generated right on your own PC — nothing about it ever leaves your local network. It just tells your phone "trust this one connection" so it can talk to your computer over Wi-Fi. It can't see or touch anything else — not your other apps, not other websites, nothing. The app doesn't send any data anywhere, ever — no analytics, no logs, no phoning home. And since it's all open-source, you don't have to take our word for it: you (or your AI coding assistant) can go read the exact code that generates this certificate right here: [`internal/ca`](https://github.com/MrHoustonOff/PhoneGyro/tree/main/pkg/ca).
setup.disclosure_body_2: **Why is this even necessary?** Safari (WebKit) simply refuses to share gyroscope/motion data or keep a live WebSocket connection open unless the page is loaded over a secure, encrypted connection (HTTPS/WSS) — that's an Apple privacy rule, and no app can get around it. Since there's no way to get a "real," publicly-trusted certificate for a private local address, self-signing one and asking your phone to trust it is the only way to satisfy that rule without ever going through the internet.
setup.disclosure_body_3: **The trade-off:** you get a fully private, direct, offline connection where none of your data ever leaves your Wi-Fi — but in exchange, you have to do this one manual "trust" step yourself, since there's no public authority that can vouch for a certificate that only exists on your home network.
setup.disclosure_body_4: No hidden actions. Just transparent local communication for your gamepad.
setup.disclosure_title: Why is this certificate needed and is it safe?
setup.ios_desc: One-time local profile setup for Safari
setup.ios_step1_text: Open the link (or scan the QR code) **on your phone**, then tap `Allow`.
setup.ios_step2_text: Go to `Settings`. A banner reading `Profile Downloaded` will appear at the top of the screen — tap it.
setup.ios_step5_text: Return to the main `Settings` screen. Go to `General` → `About`, then scroll all the way down to `Certificate Trust Settings` and tap it.
setup.ios_step6_text: You'll see your certificate listed. Toggle it on, then tap `Continue`.

settings_modal.title: Settings
settings_modal.subtitle: Server ports, network and motion filtering for advanced users
settings_modal.dsu_port_desc: UDP motion server port for emulators (default: 26760)
settings_modal.dsu_port_tip: UDP port for the Cemuhook DSU motion server. Enter this exact port in your emulator's motion settings (Cemu, RPCS3, Ryujinx, Dolphin, etc.). Default: 26760.
settings_modal.dsu_mac_tip: Persistent hardware MAC address of the virtual controller. Emulators bind motion controls directly to this address.
settings_modal.dsu_mac_regen_tip: Generate a new virtual MAC address
settings_modal.data_dir_tip: Where PhoneGyro keeps its settings, calibration profiles (USB ones in the usb subfolder), the iPhone certificate (ca), logs and window data. It cannot be moved. To reset or remove the app completely, close it and delete this folder.
settings_modal.check_updates_tip: Once per start PhoneGyro asks GitHub for the latest version number and, if a new one is out, shows a window with a download link. Nothing about you is sent. This is the only thing the app does over the internet: while it is off, PhoneGyro works fully offline.
settings_modal.dsu_mac_regen_confirm: Regenerate MAC address? Existing controller bindings in Cemu, Yuzu and other emulators will need to be re-selected.
settings_modal.http_port_tip: Local TCP port for smartphone initial pairing and iOS certificate profile download. Default: 8080.
settings_modal.https_port_tip: Secure TLS port for the controller web app. Safari requires HTTPS to access motion sensors. Default: 8443.
settings_modal.filter_live_hint: All filter adjustments apply automatically on the fly. Best tuned directly while aiming inside the game.
settings_modal.gyro_deadband_tip: Smooth deadzone: fully silences rates below the threshold (sensor noise and hand micro-tremor), and from twice the threshold passes motion unchanged, so normal aiming loses no speed. In between is a smooth, jerk-free transition. Pick the lowest threshold at which the aim stays still when you freeze.
settings_modal.gyro_sensitivity_tip: Gyro angular velocity scale factor for emulators (default: 1.00x). Scales aim speed independently of in-game sensitivity sliders.
settings_modal.gyro_deadzone_desc: Suppression of resting electronic sensor noise
settings_modal.gyro_deadzone_tip: Filters micro-noise from the phone gyro when held or resting on a desk, eliminating crosshair drift.
settings_modal.bench_sensitivity_note: Test bench response may feel different from gameplay. We **strongly recommend** tuning parameters in our app while testing directly in the game!
settings_modal.bench_offline_desc: Connect a device to view real-time response
settings_modal.bench_fs_hint: Tilt controller • Don't drop the ball! • [Esc] Exit
settings_modal.stillness_hint_tip: Show subtle recalibration hint if device rests motionless on a surface tilted by more than 10 degrees.
settings_modal.disconnect_alert_desc: Red window glow and blur when screen turns off
settings_modal.disconnect_alert_tip: Show warning card with frosted glass blur over calibration dialog if screen turns off or device disconnects.
settings_modal.silence_disconnect_desc: Drop connection after 2s of frozen or missing sensor data
settings_modal.silence_disconnect_tip: Instantly disconnect when the connection drops or sensor data freezes for 2 seconds, preventing corrupted calibration or stuck DSU output.
settings_modal.cemu_drift_guard_tip: Cemu mistakes slow motion for gyro bias and then keeps turning the aim by it, so the aim drifts even while the controller is still. The guard silently cancels that error during play. It only applies to Cemu; other emulators are unaffected.
settings_modal.minimize_to_tray_desc: Hides window to tray on close, keeping streaming active
settings_modal.minimize_to_tray_tip: When closing the window, hides it into the Windows notification area so gyro motion streaming remains uninterrupted during gameplay.
settings_modal.close_action_desc: Behavior when clicking the window close button
settings_modal.close_action_tip: Choose what happens when clicking the close button: ask each time, minimize to notification area, or terminate the application.
settings_modal.sound_mode_tip: Play an audio chime when the smartphone connects or suddenly disconnects.
settings_modal.sound_volume_tip: Adjust sound cue volume (0 - mute, 3 - maximum).
settings_modal.sound_details_desc: Individual volume control for each event
settings_modal.sound_details_tip: Expand the full list of sound effects to independently adjust volume or mute specific audio cues.
settings_modal.sound_phone_connect_tip: Triggers when the smartphone establishes a WebSocket motion connection over Wi-Fi.
settings_modal.sound_phone_disconnect_tip: Triggers when smartphone connection is lost, browser tab is closed, or screen goes to sleep.
settings_modal.sound_dsu_connect_tip: Triggers when an emulator (Cemu, Yuzu, Ryujinx, Dolphin, etc.) subscribes to Cemuhook DSU port 26760.
settings_modal.sound_recenter_desc: Neutral of the in-app 3D view locked
settings_modal.sound_recenter_tip: Triggers when orientation is recentered via global hotkey, Spacebar, or recenter modal confirm button.
settings_modal.sound_intro_desc: Short chime played on app launch
settings_modal.sound_intro_tip: Plays once when PhoneGyro opens. 0 turns it off.
settings_modal.theme_tip: Choose between dark and light appearance modes in PhoneGyro.
settings_modal.language_tip: Choose the primary display language for PhoneGyro.
settings_modal.font_scale_tip: Global font and interface scaling factor (default: 1.00x). You can also press Ctrl + and Ctrl - to adjust scale, Ctrl 0 to reset, or scroll the mouse wheel while holding Ctrl.
settings_modal.btn_reset_tip: Restore all ports and sensor parameters back to factory defaults.
settings_modal.save_notice: Saving will restart web services and reload the page
settings_modal.err_ports_duplicate: DSU, HTTP and HTTPS ports must not be identical
settings_modal.sound_link_loss_tip: A quiet cue when the link to the controller is noticeably struggling: for USB, more than 5% of frames are lost; for the phone, a link stall longer than 0.85 s or more than 60% of samples arriving merged. At most once every 15 s, never in the first 3 s after connecting or while paused. A full disconnect has its own sound. 0 turns it off.
settings_modal.deadband_off_desc: No filter: the sensor as is. For checking the sensor and debugging.
settings_modal.deadband_005_desc: A very quiet sensor resting on something (phone in a stand). Best precision for the slowest movements.
settings_modal.deadband_010_desc: Phones — iPhone and most Android. The default.
settings_modal.deadband_020_desc: A noisy phone, or playing handheld without resting your hands.
settings_modal.deadband_035_desc: The aim jitters slightly when you freeze and 0.20 is not enough.
settings_modal.deadband_050_desc: USB controller with an MPU-6050 (±2000 °/s): silences its 0.2–0.5 °/s noise. Recommended for USB.
settings_modal.deadband_075_desc: Strong hand tremor, or still shaky at 0.50. Aim adjustments slower than ~1.5 °/s get softer.
settings_modal.deadband_100_desc: Last resort: everything under 1 °/s is silenced, from 2 °/s it passes as is. Fine aim adjustment suffers.
settings_modal.gyro_deadband_usb_tip: The same for the USB controller, with its own threshold because its sensor is noisier than a phone. An MPU-6050 at ±2000 °/s has about 0.2 °/s of noise and up to 0.3–0.5 at peaks, hence the 0.50 default: the aim stays still while normal aiming (from 1 °/s) passes unchanged.
settings_modal.deadband_usb_010_desc: Too low for USB: almost all sensor noise reaches the game and the aim jitters.
settings_modal.deadband_usb_020_desc: A very quiet sensor, or one on a smaller range (±250–500 °/s).
settings_modal.deadband_usb_035_desc: Slightly softer than recommended: if 0.50 costs you slow-aim precision.
settings_modal.deadband_usb_050_desc: MPU-6050 at ±2000 °/s: silences its 0.2–0.5 °/s noise. The USB default.
